question: Icebox — ATK post-plant A, 2v2, spike down, ~0:40 on the plant. You hold an Operator scoped from A Tower onto the site. How do you play your Op in this post-plant?

options.label: Hold your scoped Op locked on the tightest defuse angle and let the clock force the defenders to come to you
options.explication_courte: Post-plant, time is on the attacker: the defenders must expose themselves to defuse. An Op pre-scoped on the one lane they have to cross converts that forced movement into a near-free pick — you make them fight your setup, not the other way around.

sources_option.citation: Holding a pre-aimed angle on the path the enemy must cross is the highest-percentage duel; make them move into your shot

options.label: Dry-peek off the Op to hunt the defenders before they group for the retake
options.explication_courte: Peeking with an Op sacrifices its whole advantage — the slow ADS and re-scope leave you exposed to a wide-swing trade. You give away your held angle and your positional edge to chase a kill the clock would have handed you.

sources_option.citation: The Operator is a holding weapon; peeking with it forfeits the pre-aim and re-scope advantage that makes it strong

options.label: Reposition off A Tower to a closer off-angle so you can swap to your sidearm if they get near the spike
options.explication_courte: Taking a fresh off-angle is a reasonable anti-pre-fire adjustment, but leaving a strong long Op perch mid-round can surrender the exact sightline that makes a defuse costly for them. Often you keep the perch and only rotate if pushed.

sources_option.citation: Repositioning to an off-angle can beat a pre-fire, but abandoning a dominant post-plant sightline can hand the defusers a free lane

options.label: Dump your ultimate and signature onto the spike immediately to zone the defuse
options.explication_courte: Blowing all your util the instant the spike lands wastes it — post-plant util is most valuable timed to the actual defuse attempt. Spending it early leaves you with nothing when they commit to the defuse with 7 seconds left.

sources_option.citation: Post-plant utility should be timed to deny the defuse itself; dumping it early leaves you empty for the moment that decides the round

explication_longue: Post-plant is the clearest place where the clock is a teammate. With the spike down in a 2v2 on A Icebox and ~40 seconds left, the defenders cannot win by waiting — they must expose themselves to reach and defuse the spike. Your job with the Operator held from A Tower is to make that forced movement as expensive as possible. Pre-scoping the tightest angle they have to cross to touch the spike converts their obligation into a near-free pick: you fight on your terms, from your setup, at the range where the Op is strongest. Dry-peeking off the Op is the costly error — you surrender its entire advantage (the slow ADS and re-scope) and expose yourself to a wide-swing trade, chasing a kill the timer would have delivered. Repositioning to a closer off-angle is a defensible anti-pre-fire tweak, but abandoning a dominant long perch mid-round can hand the defusers exactly the lane you wanted to lock; usually you keep the perch and only move if actively pushed. Dumping all your util the instant the spike lands is the faute: post-plant utility is worth most timed to the real defuse attempt, so spending it early leaves you empty at the 7-second moment that decides the round. Hold the angle, keep your util, let the clock do the work.

sources.citation: The Op is a holding weapon; pre-aim the forced lane and let the enemy move into your shot rather than peeking or repositioning away
